question: A cyclist covers 2.5 km in 4 minutes 10 seconds. How long will he take to cover 6 km at the same speed?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered = 2.5 km

Time taken = 4 minutes 10 seconds = 4 + 10/60 minutes = 4 + 1/6 minutes = 25/6 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Speed = Distance / Time

⇒ Speed = 2.5 km / (25/6 minutes)

⇒ Speed = 2.5 × (6/25) km/minute

⇒ Speed = 0.6 km/minute

To find the time to cover 6 km:

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 6 km / 0.6 km/minute

⇒ Time = 10 minutes

**The cyclist will take 10 minutes to cover 6 km at the same speed.**
